text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Alija Izetbegovic, chairman of the collective presidency, visits Turkey on Monday to discuss that country's military and political role in the peace process.

- Michael Steiner, deputy to High Representative in Bosnia, is expected to urge various political parties to hold parliament session to discuss draft customs law, one of the laws which needs to be adopted to clinch deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
- The Serb leadership in Pale is obstructing the Dayton peace accord, not the Serbs from the Moslem-Croat federation, says Haris Silajdzic, co-chairman of Council of Ministers.

- Croat Social-Liberal and other opposition parties request the Constitutional Court to revoke a decision that allows Croatian citizens in Bosnia to vote in presidential elections in Croatia scheduled this month. They say only the Croatian embassy should be permitted to accept ballots, not other venues.

-If the international donors' conference is cancelled, then the Moslem-Croat federation needs to strengthen billateral relations with countries which want to cooperate and to insist on bilateral aid so to continue reconstruction projects, Silajdzic says. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-384
